To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Chinese firms that increased their imports of intermediates also increased their exports and increased the number of export destinations; (2) the effects of imported intermediates on firm exports were greater if the intermediates were sourced from OECD countries rather than non OECD ones; (3) the effects of intermediates sourced from OECD countries were larger for private Chinese firms than for foreign invested firms; (4) the effects of imports on exports were larger for firms in industries with greater R&D intensity.

Chinese firms' import of intermediate inputs increased the volume and scope of their exports, and that the magnitude of the export benefits depended on the country of origin of the imported intermediates, the organizational form of the importing firms, and industry R D intensity.
Chinese firms that expanded their imports of intermediate inputs expanded their exports and increased the scope of their exports.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of imported inputs in the process of export upgrading.
the role of imported intermediate inputs in facilitating Chinese firms' export performance.
the role of imported intermediates in facilitating Chinese firms' export performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
imported intermediate inputs were a major factor behind China's export boom.
the empirical results in this paper show that imported intermediate inputs have a positive effect on Chinese exports.
imported intermediate inputs have a positive effect on the exports of firms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the import of intermediates is important for the export performance of Chinese firms, especially for those firms with higher technology and quality.
the import of intermediate inputs is an important channel to promote exports in China.
the Chinese government should continue to lower tariffs on imported intermediates and should also continue to encourage Chinese firms to invest in R&D and to adopt advanced technologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
China's participation in the global economy has had a positive impact on the export performance of its firms.
China's WTO entry facilitated the upgrading of Chinese firms through their imports of intermediate inputs.
imported inputs are a key driver of China's export growth and that this effect is especially important for Chinese firms in high R&D industries.
